project.name: SeaLevelLab
project.plain_summary: SeaLevelLab pulls sea-level data from three outside organisations, cleans and checks it, stores it, runs a statistical model on it, and shows the result on a map that anyone can open on a phone. Part of it updates itself every day without anyone touching it: a scheduled job calls two public data services, checks every answer before keeping it, saves it in a small database and republishes the site. If a service is down, the site keeps showing the last good data and says so.

numbers.v: live REST APIs, called daily by a scheduled job
tide gauges mapped to live stations
servers to run: static site + scheduled jobs

role: Sole developer. I chose the data sources, wrote the cleaning and the model (R / R-INLA), the Python lab (digital twin, Gymnasium environment, Bayesian optimisation, PPO, LLM agent), the live-data ETL and its database, the static web app, the tests and the CI/CD.
No team or client: the scope, the design trade-offs and the honesty notes on every page are my own decisions, recorded in the commit history and the README.

integrations.name: Pacific Sea Level and Geodetic Monitoring Project, monthly statistics
integrations.obtained: Bulk download of one monthly-statistics file per country (13 files), cleaned and merged in R into one table
integrations.frequency: One-off snapshot, 1992 to 2025 (BoM updates monthly; the model is refitted by hand)
integrations.format: Fixed-width text / CSV, one row per station-month (min, max, mean, sd, gaps)
integrations.transform: Parse, coerce to numbers, drop incomplete months, de-duplicate, attach coordinates, longitudes to 0-360; then R-INLA SPDE fit, Gaussian-process rate field and GEV on annual maxima
integrations.stored: Raw files: local only (git-ignored). Processed: Processed_Final_data.csv (committed). Model output: docs/app_data.js
integrations.used_by: R-INLA analysis, digital twin, interactive map, walkthrough, report
integrations.failure: Static snapshot; the build script stops with an error if the export is missing or the grid has the wrong size

code.note: digital twin reads the same file

integrations.notes: The country files carry no gauge coordinates; the dataset's coordinates are country-level approximations. The first cleaning pass (flood project.qmd) is an earlier local prototype that is not in the public repo.

integrations.name: UHSLC Fast Delivery hourly sea level
integrations.provider: University of Hawaii Sea Level Center, via its ERDDAP server
integrations.obtained: Scheduled ETL: one HTTPS GET per gauge to ERDDAP tabledap (.json), last 75 days
integrations.frequency: Daily job; the source lags real time by about 4-6 weeks
integrations.format: JSON table: time (UTC), sea_level (mm, gauge datum); fill value -32767
integrations.transform: Check columns, units, timestamps and value range; drop fill values; upsert by (station, hour); export the last 30 days as anomalies from their own mean
integrations.used_by: Map app: Live data tab; home page status badge; this page
integrations.failure: 30 s timeout and a 60 s cap per response, 3 retries with exponential back-off, no retry on 4xx; each gauge fetched independently; 8-minute run budget; a gauge that fails or is not reached keeps its previous export, labelled stale

code.note: 13 gauges mapped, with basis and confidence

integrations.notes: ERDDAP sends no CORS header, so a browser cannot call it directly. That is why this source has to go through a server-side job.

integrations.name: Open-Meteo Marine API, sea_level_height_msl
integrations.obtained: Scheduled ETL (daily snapshot) and a live call from the visitor's browser when they open a gauge
integrations.format: JSON: hourly time (GMT) and sea level (m, relative to global mean sea level), 7 days ahead
integrations.transform: Check units, UTC offset, array lengths and range; convert to mm; anomaly from the 7-day mean
integrations.stored: SQLite table forecasts (last 14 issues per gauge) -> docs/live/live_data.json; live result is not stored
integrations.used_by: Map app: Live data tab forecast curve
integrations.failure: ETL: same retry policy. Browser: 8 s timeout; on any error the daily snapshot stays on screen with a 'snapshot' label and the error message
integrations.notes: Modelled tides on a ~8 km grid; Open-Meteo states coastal accuracy is limited. Shown as a forecast shape only, never compared in absolute height with the gauges.

integrations.name: SQLite live database
integrations.format: Tables stations, observations, forecasts, etl_runs (status, row counts, duration, errors)
integrations.transform: Primary keys make re-runs idempotent; forecasts pruned to the last 14 issues
integrations.stored: data/live/sealevel_live.sqlite, persisted between runs in the GitHub Actions cache and attached to every run as a downloadable artifact (14 days)
integrations.used_by: The export step; the run history shown on this page
integrations.failure: If the cache is evicted the next run rebuilds it from the APIs; the site keeps the last good export meanwhile
integrations.notes: A static site has no server to hold a database, so the database lives with the job and the site reads small exports. With users writing data, this would move to a hosted Postgres behind an API.

integrations.name: Exported JSON files
integrations.obtained: Written by the ETL, committed to the repository by the workflow, served by GitHub Pages
integrations.frequency: Committed only when the data changed
integrations.format: live_data.json (~125 KB: hourly anomalies as hour offsets) and status.json (run history)
integrations.transform: Validated against the contract the front end needs; written to a temp file then renamed, so readers never see half a file
integrations.used_by: Map app, home page badge, this page
integrations.failure: If validation fails nothing is written and the previous file stays live

integrations.name: Basemap tiles
integrations.provider: Esri World Ocean Base (default); CARTO Positron and OpenStreetMap (selectable)
integrations.obtained: Tile URL templates loaded by Leaflet in the browser
integrations.failure: On tile errors the map switches to an offline coastline layer baked into app_data.js and shows a notice
integrations.notes: CARTO's free tiles now return 'API key required' watermark tiles with HTTP 200 (no error event), so Esri is the default.

integrations.name: Coastline for the offline fallback
integrations.obtained: Read once in the R build, simplified, embedded in docs/app_data.js
integrations.transform: Clip to the study box, round, drop duplicate points
integrations.used_by: Interactive map when tiles are unavailable
integrations.failure: If the package is missing the build writes an empty layer and warns

integrations.name: LLM endpoint for the lab agent
integrations.provider: Any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, a local Ollama server)
integrations.obtained: openai Python SDK (ai4s/llm_agent.py) and ellmer in R (flood_ai4s.qmd), function calling with the lab's tools
integrations.auth: OPENAI_API_KEY (+ optional OPENAI_BASE_URL) from the environment; never committed
integrations.transform: Tools return compact JSON summaries; tool inputs are validated and errors returned as text the model can re-plan from
integrations.used_by: Python demo (run_demo.py --live) and the R notebook's live-agent chunk
integrations.failure: The default is a deterministic mock agent that drives the same tools with no key (used in CI); the LLM agent is opt-in (--live), and the R chunk is skipped when no key is set

integrations.name: GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages
integrations.obtained: Workflows in .github/workflows; Pages serves docs/ from main
integrations.auth: Workflow token scoped to this repository (contents: write, pages: write for the ETL only)
integrations.frequency: CI on every push; ETL daily at 03:17 UTC and on demand
integrations.transform: CI runs the Gymnasium checker and closed-loop tests, the ETL tests and the browser-formula tests
integrations.stored: Run logs and the database artifact on GitHub
integrations.failure: A failed ETL marks the run red and keeps the last good data live

request_flow.title: What happens when you open a gauge's Live data tab

steps.what: You click a gauge on the map and open the Live data tab.
The page loads live/live_data.json once (same site, ~125 KB, cached for the session). It was produced by last night's ETL run.
It draws the last 30 days of hourly gauge readings (UHSLC) as an SVG line, with the retrieval time and a link to the exact API query.
It draws the 7-day forecast from the snapshot straight away, then asks Open-Meteo for a fresh forecast directly from your browser (8 s timeout).
The answer is checked (units, UTC, lengths, range) before it replaces the snapshot. On any failure the snapshot stays and the label says why.
Behind it, every night: GitHub Actions runs the tests, restores the database, calls both APIs for 13 gauges, upserts, exports, and commits only if the data changed.

reliability.d: Every server-side call has a 30 s timeout, a hard 60 s cap on the whole response, and up to 3 retries with exponential back-off; client errors (4xx) are not retried. The whole run has an 8-minute budget: gauges not reached keep their last good data. The browser call has an 8 s timeout.
Responses are checked for columns, units, time zone, timestamps and plausible ranges. A response that fails is rejected whole, not partly stored.
Each gauge and each provider is fetched independently: one failing station does not stop the other twelve.
Exports are validated, written atomically, and committed only when the data changed. If a refresh fails the previous data stays on the site, labelled stale.
Primary keys on (station, hour) make re-running a day harmless; tests check that a second run changes nothing.
Every run is logged in the database (status, row counts, duration, errors) and summarised in status.json, which drives the badge on the home page and the run history below.

security.d: The two live APIs need no key. The LLM key is read from the environment on the developer's machine and never committed.
The ETL workflow's token can write only to this repository's contents and Pages; CI has read-only access.
UHSLC data: free use, not for legal use (stated in the UI). Open-Meteo: non-commercial free tier, CC BY 4.0 attribution on every chart.

roadmap: Roadmap: refit the INLA model monthly from the accumulating UHSLC series, so the risk map moves with the data.
Roadmap: an alert when a gauge's observed anomaly exceeds its 1-in-N level (needs a datum tie between UHSLC and the BoM series).

delivery.intro: How I would take your platform from idea to launch without an in-house tech lead. Each step lists what I do, what you see, and where the same step is visible in my own work.

stages.do: Agree the users, the one job the first release must do, and what is out of scope. Write down data owners and constraints.
stages.see: A one-page scope and a list of open decisions with who owns each.

evidence.label: Decisions written into the site itself: what the probability means and does not mean

stages.do: Pick the simplest stack that meets the need, and say what would make us change it.
stages.see: A short architecture note: components, hosting, costs, and the trigger for the next step up.

evidence.label: Static site + scheduled job + SQLite instead of a server, and when that would change (this page)

stages.do: List every external system, how we call it, auth, limits, failure handling and licence, before writing code against it.
stages.see: An integrations table like the one on this page, kept in the repository.

evidence.label: Gauge mapping with basis and confidence

stages.do: Ship something usable every few days, each change small enough to review and roll back.
stages.see: A working link after every release, not a big reveal at the end.

evidence.label: Commit history: each commit is one shippable change

stages.do: Automated tests on every push for the parts that would hurt if they broke: data parsing, maths, failure paths.
stages.see: A green check on every change; failures block the release.

stages.do: Automated deploys, scheduled jobs, a visible health indicator, and a rollback point before every major change.
stages.see: A status indicator and a run history you can check without asking me.

stages.do: A README that runs from a clean machine, plain-language pages for non-technical readers, and no knowledge that lives only in my head.
stages.see: Someone else can run, change and deploy it.

stages.t: Working with specialists, no tech lead
stages.do: Turn technical choices into short options with costs for you to decide; give designers, content owners and vendors clear inputs and deadlines; flag risks early in writing.
stages.see: Weekly written update: done, next, decisions needed from you, risks.

evidence.label: Honesty notes on data limits, written for non-specialists

first_two_weeks.t: Read everything that exists; talk to you and each specialist; list users, the first release's one job, systems to integrate, and open decisions.
Architecture note and integrations table; test access to each third-party system (keys, sandboxes, rate limits, CORS).
Repository, CI, staging deploy and a skeleton site live on a link you can open. First weekly update.
First end-to-end slice: one real user flow, through one real integration, into the database and back to the screen, with tests and monitoring. Demo on Friday; agree the next slice.

probes.label: Open-Meteo: 7-day sea-level forecast for Funafuti, Tuvalu
probes.why: Open-Meteo allows calls from any web page (CORS: *), so the map refreshes the forecast live.
probes.done: this is the same call the map makes when you open a gauge

probes.label: UHSLC: last 50 days of hourly readings at Funafuti, called straight from this page
probes.why: UHSLC's server does not send a CORS header, so browsers refuse to hand the answer to a web page. This is why the gauges come through the nightly server-side job instead.
